memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "They made the ephod of gold, and of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of finely twisted linen. They hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut strands to be worked into the blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen - the work of skilled hands." - Exod 39:2-3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a remarkable piece of craftsmanship. Gold was hammered into sheets so thin that it could be cut into threads, then woven right into the fabric.

Think about what that took. Patient beating, again and again, until solid metal became something flexible enough to be worked into cloth. Gold that stayed in a lump would have been useless for this garment.

There is a picture here of how God often works with us. Pressure applied over time is not always destruction; sometimes it is preparation. What feels like being flattened may be God making us usable in a way we could not have been before.

Peter says our faith is refined by fire so that it may result in praise, glory and honour when Christ is revealed (1 Pet 1:6-7). James says the testing of our faith produces perseverance (Jas 1:2-4).

Notice also that the gold thread ran through the whole garment. Not a gold badge pinned on top — gold woven all the way through the fabric.

That is what God is doing in us. Not adding a religious layer to an unchanged life, but working something precious through the whole of it, thread by thread.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What pressure are you under that God might be using to make you usable?
2. Is your faith a layer on top of your life or woven through it?
3. Where have you seen something valuable come out of a hard season?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, when I feel hammered thin, remind me that You are making me useful. Weave Yourself through all of me. Amen.
